subject: Re: Long-context evals & model recommendations — post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Long-context evals & model recommendations — post-call recap

Thanks John & Sarah — great conversation today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and success criteria for the long-context evaluation.

TL;DR
- Goal: validate model fit for ACME’s 50k-token case (multi-document legal summaries + entity extraction).
- Primary concerns: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity across section boundaries, and latency at 8k vs 32k vs >=64k contexts.
- Recommended initial models: Llama-3-70B-32k-quant (fast baseline), RedWind-1.2-64k (higher-fidelity), and a distilled 16B variant for throughput tests.

What we shared today (attached/links):
- Redwood long-context benchmark report (attached: redwood_benchmark_report.pdf) — shows truncation failure modes and summary drift across 32k+ examples.
- Prompt sets (linked) with representative ACME docs (contract bundles + case notes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-sets/blob/main/acme-long-context.json
- Raw eval results CSV (attached: long_context_eval_results.csv) with per-example token counts, ROUGE, and custom fidelity scores.

Technical notes / areas to validate in the POC:
1) Truncation policy: we recommend testing three strategies — prefix-only, sliding-window summarization, and automatic chunk summarizer with overlapping context. We’ll instrument per-token provenance to see where important facts fall out.
2) Summarization fidelity: measure hallucination/omission on a 200-item prompt set. We flagged examples in the CSV where named-entities were dropped after 16k tokens.
3) Cost/latency: run throughput tests on Dedicated capacity vs Hosted API; we’ll surface per-token cost deltas and recommend batching sizes.

Next steps (proposed):
1) ACME to confirm the canonical dataset subset for the 200-item fidelity run (deadline: Fri 2026-03-06).
2) Redwood to spin up three model variants and run a 200-item pass with metric outputs + per-example logs (ETA: 3 business days after dataset confirmation).
3) Joint review call to go over results & decide on rollout strategy (30–45 min) — propose Tue 2026-03-10 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_report.pdf, long_context_eval_results.csv, prompt_sets_v1.json (the GitHub link above mirrors the prompt set).

If that all looks right, I’ll create the shared Drive folder (linked) and send over a DocuSign SOW for the POC.

—
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks John. Quick answers inline and then logistics: 

1) Dataset & redaction: good to know — please flag which examples are redacted vs not in the drive subset. We’ll treat redacted examples as higher priority for hallucination regression checks.

2) Chunking ownership: Redwood can manage chunking and the overlapping-window summarizer — our default is to run chunking server-side so ACME does not have to change ingestion. If you prefer pre-processing in your environment for data governance, we can provide the exact chunking code (open-source gist / small container).

POC SOW items:
- Dedicated capacity estimate (3-day run): ~ 48 GPU-hours on A100/80GB equiv — preliminary cost estimate attached as a line item in the SOW (I’ll send with DocuSign).
- Provenance retention: we can retain per-token provenance logs for 90 days; if you need longer retention we can add an archival option (additional charge).

I’ve created the shared Drive folder and uploaded the prompt set + a small README with recommended evaluation config: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCexampleLink

Neha (cc) will coordinate the eval run once you confirm the dataset subset. We’ll queue the three model variants and share results + per-example logs.

See you on Tue 3/10 — I’ll include a calendar invite in a follow-up.

—
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Hi John & team — looping in the run plan and quick checklist so we can start as soon as ACME confirms the 200-item set: 

Run plan (high level):
- Day 0: Ingest dataset subset into a private S3 (or we can accept upload to our secure Drive) and validate checksums.
- Day 1: Run three model variants: Llama-3-70B-32k-quant (baseline), RedWind-1.2-64k (high-fidelity), Redwood-Distill-16B (throughput test). Collect ROUGE/ROUGE-L, exact-match for key entities, and our custom fidelity score.
- Day 2: Run chunking strategies (prefix-only, sliding-window, chunk-summarizer) on flagged long examples and collect per-strategy metrics.
- Day 3: Consolidate results, generate per-example provenance logs, and produce a summary deck for the joint review.

Checklist:
- Confirm dataset subset link in Drive by 2026-03-06 (ACME)
- Confirm acceptance of 48 GPU-hour estimate or request alternate sizing (ACME)
- NDA/SOW signature (if ACME legal needs it we can expedite)

Attachments/links: prompt_sets_v1.json, redwood_benchmark_report.pdf, long_context_eval_results.csv

If you’d like, we can include a short automated regression test that flags any summaries with entity-drop > 2 per document — that’s useful long-term to detect quality regressions.

Thanks — Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
